name: Nice
tagline: French Riviera Elegance Where the Alps Meet the Sea
description: Nice is the jewel of the French Riviera, combining Mediterranean beaches, Belle Époque architecture, and a world-class culinary scene with the cultural depth of France. It is significantly more expensive than Eastern or Southern European alternatives, but the quality of life, healthcare, infrastructure, and sheer beauty are among the best in the world. The Promenade des Anglais, the old town markets, and proximity to Monaco and the Alps make Nice an aspirational FIRE destination.

quickFacts.visa: Schengen visa (90 days); Long-Stay Visa for retirees available
quickFacts.language: French, English spoken in tourist areas and by younger generation
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate-High – safe city with typical tourist-area precautions
quickFacts.climate: Mediterranean with warm dry summers and mild winters

housing.description: Studio or small 1-bedroom inland-north (Libération, Saint-Roch, Riquier, northern hills), off the coast

dining.description: Mostly home cooking plus a few cheap meals

healthcare.description: Solid individual private/international plan for age ~50

transportation.description: Lignes d'Azur adult monthly pass; no car

1M.lifestyle: A studio or small one-bedroom inland in Libération, Saint-Roch, or the northern hills, away from the coast, with a Lignes d'Azur tram-and-bus pass and no car. Most meals are cooked at home, with socca, pan bagnat, and pizza from Vieux Nice stands for cheap outings. Health cover is an entry private/international plan pitched at the long-stay visa requirement. The apartment is modest and dining out is occasional, but the beaches, the Cours Saleya market, and the Promenade des Anglais cost nothing.

housing.description: Proper 1-bedroom on the edge of the centre or a good-quality inland flat

healthcare.description: Better individual international plan, lower deductible

entertainment.description: More dining out, events, day trips

2M.lifestyle: A proper one-bedroom on the edge of the centre or a good inland flat, dining out regularly at casual and mid-range spots. Health cover improves to a lower-deductible international plan, and there is room for day trips, events, and a gym. Comfortable Riviera living a short ride from the sea.

housing.description: Good 1-bedroom in a desirable area (Musicians' Quarter, Le Port, lower Cimiez), walkable to the sea

transportation.description: Transit pass plus regular rideshare/occasional rental car

3M.lifestyle: A good one-bedroom in a desirable area — the Musicians' Quarter, Le Port, or lower Cimiez — walkable to the water. Dining out is frequent, health cover is a comprehensive international plan, and the tram pass plus regular rideshare or an occasional rental car cover the coast. Culture, concerts, and weekend excursions to Monaco, Èze, or the Alps are routine, with real margin left over.

housing.description: Spacious 1–2 bedroom with a sea view near the Carré d'Or or on the Cimiez heights

transportation.description: Car appears here (ownership/lease, fuel, parking) plus taxis

luxuryExtras.description: Beach-club/gym membership, wine, occasional yacht day

5M.lifestyle: A spacious one- or two-bedroom with a sea view near the Carré d'Or or on the Cimiez heights, with a weekly cleaner. Dining is frequent and fine, a premium international plan removes friction, and a car appears for the first time alongside taxis. A beach-club or gym membership, events, and frequent travel round out upper-affluent Riviera life.

housing.description: Belle Époque apartment in the Carré d'Or or Cimiez, or a villa on Mont Boron with sea views

transportation.description: Luxury car plus occasional driver and helicopter transfers to Monaco

luxuryExtras.description: Yacht charters, private-club dues, concierge, luxury travel

10M.lifestyle: A Belle Époque apartment in the Carré d'Or or Cimiez, or a villa on Mont Boron with sea views, kept by a housekeeper and part-time staff. Dining runs to Michelin and haute cuisine, health cover is top-tier international concierge, and a luxury car with an occasional driver and helicopter transfers to Monaco handle transport. The discretionary budget funds yacht charters, private-club dues, galas, and luxury travel — the genuinely lavish Riviera lifestyle the Côte d'Azur is famous for.
